items.title: SA government advertising spend hits record levels

children.content: The Malinauskas government has spent nearly $200 million on advertising in its first four years in office, including a record spend last financial year.

items.title: Bird flu adds to fears for threatened species at proposed wind farm site

children.content: Victorian ecologists are warning of the "compounding risks" of bird flu and a proposal for the nation's tallest wind turbines on threatened species.

items.title: Driver arrested for allegedly ramming rideshare vehicle, road closed after hills crash

children.content: A 19-year-old driver who allegedly rammed a rideshare vehicle has been arrested. Meanwhile after a separate incident, road closures are in place after a fatal crash at Paracombe, north-east of Adelaide.

image.altText: Uniformed police officers stand around a silver sedan, with one officer pointing to the distance

items.title: Basin communities feeling drained as more water buybacks considered

children.content: The federal government has not ruled out using more water buybacks to make up a shortfall in a key Murray-Darling Basin Plan water-saving target.

items.title: Farmer fined $60k for clearing native vegetation north of Adelaide

children.content: A 73-year-old farmer is fined $60,000 for clearing more than 250 hectares of native vegetation at a property at Port Wakefield.

image.altText: A green low-lying samphire plant

items.title: Short-stay operators have mixed reactions to SA's register proposal

children.content: The scheme is still being shaped but some operators are raising concerns about security and giving local governments control over land use and deciding rates.

image.altText: A man with hat stands in front on a modern short term rental property in a regional area.

items.title: SA's first musical theatre company brings talent home in debut stage

children.content: Performers like Joey Haenen and Jazz Garcia who sought opportunities on the east coast are returning to Adelaide in Full Circle's debut production of SA's first musical theatre company.

image.altText: Joey Haenen surrounded by other performers during a production

items.title: SA government says prior parklands works set precedent for MotoGP circuit

children.content: The city O-Bahn tunnel and new Women's and Children's Hospital have set precedents for major work in the Adelaide parklands, the state government has argued in a MotoGP circuit assessment.

image.altText: a drone shot of Victoria Park with an Adelaide sign on the road

items.title: Harvest starts on SA crops that 'have not had a setback all season'

children.content: South Australia's crops, sown early on the back of good autumn rain, are ready for harvest. Logistically, it is going to be a big, difficult harvest but "what a great problem" to have, says a grower.

items.title: Regional audiences to lose Network 10, as licensee warns of TV's future

children.content: After a three-month reprieve, WIN confirms Network 10 will go from Mount Gambier, the Riverland and Griffith.

image.altText: Sign of the number 10 in a blue circle on a brown wall

items.title: Diseases of the past like measles and diphtheria are making a comeback

children.content: A recent outbreak of measles in Adelaide has sparked concern from health authorities, but it's not the only infectious illness where cases are rising once again.

image.altText: A young girl receives a vaccination from a man in a white coat in an undated black and white photograph.

items.title: The 'brutal' act that changed Alastair Campbell's opinion of Britain's new PM

children.content: The Rest Is Politics podcast co-host and former adviser to Tony Blair says he is now "moderately" hopeful Britain can put a decade of political turmoil behind it.

items.title: Public supermarkets could slash food bills by quarter, Greens think tank says

children.content: Taking inspiration from New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, "Fair Go Grocers" public supermarkets would offer essential goods at a discount and act as a competitor to drive down prices at Coles and Woolworths.

image.altText: The outside of a Woolworths supermarket. People walk in the entrance.

children.content: Sophisticated fraudsters posing as recruiters and using other dubious tactics are taking advantage of desperate jobseekers after announcing they're #opentowork.

children.content: Workers in the world's largest gig economy are being paid as little as $45 a day and sometimes going months without a day off. The ABC hears from one of them.

items.title: Nobel medicine prize awarded to scientists for brain activity research

children.content: The prize went to scientists working on the mechanisms the brain uses to switch the activity of individual nerve cells on or off.

items.title: Teenager loses hand as French student protests escalate

children.content: A 15-year-old student has lost a hand picking up a police grenade as part of nationwide protests in France over classroom conditions that have disrupted lessons at hundreds of schools since last week.

children.content: The 27-year-old horse was found with a gunshot wound in a paddock in Lovely Banks last month.

children.content: The waterway in the Red Sea, which facilitates about 12 per cent of global trade, was seized by the Houthis last month.

items.title: Shopper told youths were 'waiting for him' after shoplifting accusation

items.title: 'People can overdose and die within minutes': Alert raised over synthetic opioid

children.content: Health authorities in Tasmania have issued a public warning after an overdose death that may have been brought about by drugs "possibly laced with a strong opioid".

items.title: Bank of America met with Australian super funds and delivered a warning

children.content: Interest rates are approaching levels that would hurt Australia's economy and the retirement savings managed by major superannuation funds, according to the Bank of America's head of interest rates strategy.

image.altText: The US flag is flying on the side of a building with a blurred street sign for Wall St in the foreground.

items.title: Property downturn deepens with less than 50pc of auctions leading to a sale

children.content: Australia's auction clearance rate has slumped to a three-month low, while new data shows the number of unsold homes has surged by more than 20 per cent in the past year.

image.altText: A yellow flag that says "open home" flying off a yellow real estate sign advertising an auction.

children.content: The push comes amid growing ethical and privacy concerns around the new devices, which have been marketed by technology giants such as Meta.

items.title: IS-linked Australians in Iraq face 'risk of unfair prosecution', HRW warns

items.title: Former Bachelor star Sam Wood will stay behind bars after facing court on DV charges

children.content: The Tasmanian government has effectively been leasing out a stadium to property developer and NBL owner Larry Kestelman for less than it would cost to rent most houses in the area, a parliamentary report has found.
